title: JSON Schema Studio — Live Validation & Example Generation
description: Edit a JSON Schema written in a draft 2020-12 subset (types, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, numeric bounds, lengths, patterns, oneOf/anyOf/allOf and recursive $ref into $defs) and watch sample documents validate as you type. Every error carries a JSON Pointer to the failing value and another to the failing keyword. Generate a valid example straight from the schema, and start from Order, Payment, Tree or Config presets.
prompt: Build 'JSON Schema Studio'. Let me edit a JSON Schema in a subset of draft 2020-12: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, min/max, minLength/maxLength, pattern, oneOf/anyOf/allOf, and $ref to $defs. Validate sample JSON documents live, with precise error paths and messages. Generate a valid example document from the schema, and include presets. No libraries: write the validator yourself. Design it like a Swiss poster: off-white, black, one signal red, big numerals.

methodology: Golden error lists: each broken preset document is asserted as an ordered list of (instance pointer, failing keyword) pairs, which pins both the validator's semantics and its traversal order.
Keyword-location precision: full schema pointers through $ref hops (for example #/$ref/properties/children/items/$ref/…/minLength) are asserted for a recursive tree.

Spec edge cases chosen from draft 2020-12: 1.0 counts as an integer, lengths count code points, patterns are unanchored, oneOf reports 'none' and 'more than one' differently, and unknown keywords are surfaced rather than silently trusted.
Round-trip property: for every preset, the generated example must validate against its own schema, and loading it into a failing document tab turns that tab valid.
Resilience: malformed schema or document JSON produces a readable message and aria-invalid instead of an exception; edits persist through reload and Reset restores the preset.
risks: Infinite recursion through $ref cycles; validation has a depth guard, and generation stops adding optional properties past a depth.
The pattern-to-string generator only handles simple regexes, so exotic patterns may produce an example that fails; the page then says so rather than claiming success.
Error ordering changing with object key order, which the golden tests would catch.
Long pointers and patterns overflowing narrow screens (handled with overflow-wrap:anywhere).
qa.playwright: The validator's output is mirrored into data-ip and data-kp attributes on each error row, so tests compare exact JSON Pointers instead of parsing prose, and a compact 'pointer keyword' projection keeps the golden lists readable. Textareas are driven with fill(), which fires the same input event as typing, so live validation, persistence and aria-invalid are all exercised. The generator is checked through its own re-validation flag (data-valid) across all four presets in a loop. Nothing is time-based or random, and no screenshots are compared.
coverage: Order preset: nine ordered errors, schema pointer through $ref, minItems
Live schema and document editing, invalid JSON, unsupported keywords, integer 1.0, persistence and reset
oneOf: two matches versus none, with the closest branch
Recursive $ref deep paths; allOf plus anyOf failures
Generate for all presets and load the example into a failing tab

a11y: Both editors are labelled textareas that set aria-invalid on malformed JSON, the verdict and generator result are live regions, and document tabs expose their valid or invalid state as text as well as a coloured dot. Errors are an ordered list, with each JSON Pointer given as text.
